28 Ways AI Gets Billed: The Full List
entries.summary: Every pricing mechanism I can document across 106 models from 18 vendors, ranked from most common to most obscure, with what to watch, how to optimize and what to avoid for each one.
entries.intro: I track 106 priced models from 18 vendors. Across them I count 28 distinct ways a vendor turns usage into a charge. Two are close to universal. Everything else is a twist on those two meters, and the twists are where budgets break. Here is the full list, most common first.

list.name: Per Input and Output Token
list.line: The vendor prices input and output tokens separately, per million. Every tracked model uses it.

list.name: Cached Input Read Discount
list.line: When a request reuses a prompt prefix the vendor already holds in cache, those tokens bill at a cache-hit price below the normal input price.

list.name: Per-Call Server Tool Fees
list.line: When the vendor runs a tool on its own servers, such as web search, it charges per call or per 1,000 calls.

list.name: Separate Cache Write Charge
list.line: The vendor bills the cache write as its own line, separate from cached reads.

list.name: Batch Discount
list.line: You submit work asynchronously and accept a delay, typically up to 24 hours. Batch cuts the price in half on 39 tracked models.

list.name: Free Tiers and $0 Price Lines
list.line: The vendor prices a model, a unit or a usage band at zero, either permanently or for a limited time.

list.name: Speed, Priority and "Highspeed" Tiers
list.line: You pay more for faster output or for priority admission. OpenAI Ultrafast reaches 6x standard.

list.name: Container and Session Runtime Fees
list.line: The vendor charges by time for a sandbox or an agent session, separately from tokens.

list.name: Data Residency and Regional Price Lists
list.line: The vendor adds a surcharge to keep processing inside a named geography, or publishes a separate price list for each region.

list.name: Prompt-Size (Long Context) Bands
list.line: When the prompt crosses a threshold, the whole request reprices at a higher band. 22 tracked models do this.

list.name: Cache Write Priced by Retention Time (TTL)
list.line: The longer the vendor holds the cache, the more the write costs.

list.name: Flex (Slow, Cheap Synchronous) Tier
list.line: The request stays synchronous but accepts slower or interruptible service in exchange for a batch-like discount.

list.name: Hidden Token Overhead
list.line: These are tokens you pay for but did not write: tool system prompts, tool definitions, tokenizer changes and fixed blocks.

list.name: Reasoning (Thinking) Tokens Billed as Output
list.line: Internal reasoning tokens bill at the output price, even when the vendor hides or encrypts them.

list.name: Cache and File Storage by Time
list.line: The vendor charges to keep data available, priced per token-hour or per GB-day.

list.name: Promotional Pricing and Dated Step-Ups
list.line: The vendor publishes a price with an announced end date, or schedules an increase in advance.

list.name: Time-of-Day and Day-of-Week Bands
list.line: The same model costs different amounts depending on when the request runs.

list.name: Legacy Model Names Billed as a Different Model
list.line: An old model name keeps working, but a different model serves the request and sets the bill.

list.name: Per Image, Per Second, Per Minute, Per Character
list.line: The vendor prices media outside the token meter, or converts each asset into a fixed number of tokens.

list.name: Fine-Tuning, Training and Fine-Tuned Inference
list.line: The vendor charges for training, then charges a higher inference price for the customized model.

list.name: Subscription With Bundled, Rationed Usage
list.line: The customer pays a flat monthly fee that includes usage measured in opaque limits instead of tokens.

list.name: Per-User License and Bring-Your-Own-Key Fees
list.line: The customer pays a fixed fee per user, or pays a platform fee when it supplies its own vendor API key (bring your own key, or BYOK).

list.name: Minimums, Top-Ups and Expiring Prepaid Balances
list.line: Vendors set spend floors, require unlock payments and let prepaid balances lapse.

list.name: Commits, Take-or-Pay and Negotiated Volume Discounts
list.line: The customer promises to spend a set amount in return for a lower price, and the vendor still bills any unused commitment.

list.name: Marketplace Consumption Units
list.line: The vendor prices usage in dollars, then converts it into the marketplace's own billing unit.

list.name: Data-for-Discount Tiers
list.line: The vendor lowers the price in exchange for the right to use your data.

list.name: Billing-Event Rules
list.line: These rules decide which events are billable, separate from the price itself.

list.name: Resale Markup and Reseller Chains
list.line: A reseller prices on top of vendor cost, and resellers can sit under other resellers.
